title: Supporting roles and decoder failure boundaries
description: Terms for retaining course-owned model decisions, exact dependency observations and precise state effects after failure.

terms.definition: Work around the decoder, such as reading native settings or hashing supplied bytes. Its permitted call role leaves taught attention, tokenization, gradients and optimizer decisions in course Rust.

The independently approved package, edge, feature and role records for one fixed build context. Structural match requires no added records and no missing records; a broader permission catalog is a separate input.

The specific supporting operation permitted at a source call. Binding its reviewed source bytes detects drift; matching hashes or package names do not decide whether the call hides a taught model operation.

A condition the existing decoder validator requires, such as positive head count and compatible head grouping. Reading settings syntax does not establish that the resulting model is valid or executable.

The continuation rule attached to a typed failure: reject unchanged, discard provisional work, or stop the affected session or job. Its state promise applies at the declared operation boundary, not to every earlier successful update.

The explicit outcome of a failed operation: rejected, failed, cancelled or timed out. It is recorded separately from the reason and disposition; a later cancellation does not retract an already committed result.

Candidate output or owned payload that has not crossed its commit point. The local fixture can discard it while retaining committed counters; a failed cleanup instead reports retained ownership and forbids reuse.

Separate bindings for the configuration requested and the implementation actually selected. Before selection, actual identity remains not_selected; an available substitute does not silently become the requested backend.
